from torchvision import transforms

def count_stove_burners(image_path):
    # Convert the image to RGB
    transform = transforms.Compose([transforms.ColorJitter(brightness=60, contrast=60, saturation=60, hue=60),
                                    transforms.ToTensor()])
    image = image_path
    transform_image = transform(image)

    # Detect the stove burners using the Grounding DINO model
    detection_output = []
    result = object_detection_tool.detect(transform_image)
    for object_info in result["output"]:
        if "name" in object_info and object_info["name"] == "stove burner" and "confidence score" in object_info:
            # Get the bounding box of the stove burner
            box = tuple([bounding_box["x_min"] for bounding_box in object_info["bbox"] if bounding_box["name"] == "stove burner"])
            # Extract the label name for the stove burner
            label_name = "stove burner" if "name" in object_info else "stove"
            detection_output.append({"label": label_name, "confidence score": object_info["confidence score"], "box": box})

    # Convert the obtained data to a list of dictionaries
    detection_output = [{"label": "stove burner", "confidence score": detection_output[0]["confidence score"], "box": detection_output[0]["box"]}]

    # Check the confidence score and add empty padding if needed
    detection_output = [{"label": "stove burner", "confidence score": confidence_score, "box": bounding_box} for confidence_score, bounding_box in detection_output if confidence_score > 0.7]

    # Return the final result without empty padding
    final_result = [{"label": "stove burner", "confidence score": detection_output[0]["confidence score"], "box": detection_output[0]["box"]}]

    return final_result

#include "opencv2/opencv.hpp"
#include "dino_detector.hpp"

using namespace DinoDetector;

// Function to detect the number of burners in an image
int detectBurnersInImage(cv::Mat image, int threshold, cv::ModelSize modelSize, int padding) {
    int burnersCount = 0;
    // Load the image
    cv::Mat img = cv::imread(image);
    // Initialize the model with the given model size and threshold
    Model model = Model::createModel(modelSize, threshold, false);
    // Detect the burners in the image
    std::vector<Point2f> positions;
    Mat detectedBurners = model.detect(img, positions);
    // Iterate over the detected positions and count the burners
    for (int i = 0; i < positions.size(); ++i) {
        if (positions[i].x > 80 && positions[i].y > 100) {
            ++burnersCount;
        }
    }
    // Add empty padding around detected burners
    for (int i = 0; i < positions.size(); ++i) {
        // Extract the X and Y coordinates
        int x = positions[i].x - padding;
        int y = positions[i].y - padding;
        // Calculate the width and height of the detected burner
        int w = x + (int)std::abs(positions[i].x - img.cols + std::maximum(0, positions[i].x - img.cols + padding));
        int h = y + (int)std::abs(positions[i].y - img.nrows +  std::maximum(0, positions[i].y - img.nrows + padding));
        // Add padding around the detected burner
        img.at<uchar>(y, x) = 1;
    }
    return burnersCount;
}

int main() {
    // Read the input image
    cv::Mat image;
    // Convert the input image to grayscale
    cv::.imread(image, cv::IMREAD_GRAYSCALE);
    // Detect burners in the image
    int burnersCount = detectBurnersInImage(image, 0.35, cv::ModelSize::MIN(), 15);
    // Calculate the temperature of the stovetop
    for (int i = 0; i < burnersCount; ++i) {
        for (int j = 0; j < burnersCount; ++j) {
            // Print the detected burner's label
            std::cout << "Burner " << i+1 << "(" << j+1 << ") detected in the Stovetop." << std::endl;
        }
    }
    return 0;
}

from object_detector_tool import *
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

def detect_objects(image_path, labels, threshold=0.35, model_size="tiny", padding=20):
    # Load object detector model
    detection_tool = Object_Detector_Tool(image_path, labels, threshold, model_size, padding)
    detection_result = detection_tool.execute()

    # Filter objects
    def filter_objects(object):
        x0, y0, w, h = object[3:7]
        score = object[0]
        return (h >= 20) and (w >= 20) and (score >= 0.2)

    filtered_objects = [i for i in detection_result['output'] if filter_objects(i)]

    # Print detected objects information
    if filtered_objects:
        print(f"Detected objects with labels {'',}'.join([' '.join(detection_result['label']) for detection in filtered_objects]), "with confidence score >= 0.2, box coordinates (x0, y0), width (w), and height (h):")
        print(filtered_objects)

    # Display detected objects with empty padding
    plt.figure(figsize=(10, 7))
    plt.imshow(detector_tool.image, cmap='gray')
    for i, detection in enumerate(filtered_objects):
        x0, y0, w, h = detection
        plt.gca().axes.set_yticklabels([])
        plt.gca().axes.set_xticks([])
        plt.gca().text(x0, y0, f"label {labels[i]} with confidence {score[i]:.1f}.", va="center", ha="center", horizontalalignment="center", verticalalignment="center")
        plt.gca().add_patch(image.Rectangle((x0, y0), w, h, fill=False))

    plt.show()
